name: Genpact

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Genpact Logo Black (3).png, commons.wikimedia.org; saved as the 500 px thumbnail, 500x263)

description: Genpact runs back-office and operations processes for large companies and increasingly sells data, AI and 'agentic' software work on top. It began as General Electric's internal shared-services center and still earns most of its money from running finance and accounting, procurement, supply-chain, insurance claims, customer care and similar processes for clients, billed on time-and-material, per-resource, per-transaction or fixed-price terms. Core Business Services (decision support, technology services, digital operations) were 76.3 percent of 2025 revenue and Advanced Technology Solutions (data and AI, digital technology, advisory, agentic) 23.7 percent. Revenue was $5.08 billion in 2025 with over 146,500 employees, and no customer is more than 10 percent of revenue.

sub.name: IT and management consulting and back-office outsourcing

gics.note: Per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 400 companies' (raw wikitext read 2026-10-27; Genpact has been in the S&P MidCap 400 since May 3, 2021). Note the contrast with EPAM, which the same source puts in Information Technology / IT Consulting & Other Services, although EPAM names Genpact as a competitor. That list gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry are null.

hq.note: Principal executive office on the FY2025 10-K cover is Canon's Court, 22 Victoria Street, Hamilton, Bermuda. Wikipedia's S&P 400 list shows the headquarters as New York City; see conflicts.

employees.note: "over 146,500 employees" serving clients from more than 35 countries (FY2025 10-K Item 1)

businessLines.name: High Tech and Manufacturing
businessLines.how: Clients pay for people and technology that run their processes, billed per hour, per resource, per transaction or at a fixed price under multi-year master agreements; Genpact keeps part of the productivity gains.
businessLines.description: Clients in high tech hardware and software, digital platforms, social media, semiconductors, media and communications; and aerospace, automotive, chemicals, energy, industrial machinery, logistics, oil and gas and utilities. Services include trust and safety, advertising sales support, customer care, supply chain, procurement and engineering services.

operatingProfit.note: Segment adjusted income from operations (AOI, non-GAAP); FY2024 $319.4M. About 40.7% of the $909.5M segment total before unallocated corporate items

businessLines.name: Consumer and Healthcare
businessLines.how: Same process-outsourcing contract model as above, billed by transaction, resource or fixed price, with healthcare claims and revenue-cycle work paid on volume processed.
businessLines.description: Clients in consumer goods, retail, life sciences, healthcare payers and providers. Services include demand and supply planning, order management, trade promotion, regulatory affairs for life sciences, and claims lifecycle management and revenue cycle management for healthcare.

operatingProfit.note: Segment AOI (non-GAAP); FY2024 $293.1M. About 32.4% of the segment total

businessLines.name: Financial Services
businessLines.how: Same process-outsourcing model; insurance clients also pay for the company's own policy-administration software and for third-party claims administration.
businessLines.description: Banking, capital markets and insurance clients: onboarding, customer service, collections, loan operations, payments, insurance policy administration, underwriting support and claims, plus a proprietary insurance policy suite.

operatingProfit.note: Segment AOI (non-GAAP); FY2024 $215.9M. About 26.8% of the segment total

brands.share: Single brand; no separately reported brands
